key_insight: VLM-IE3D makes standard vision-language models more 3D-aware by adding learned geometric representations from RGB videos. This helps the model reason better about spatial relationships, depth, and object layout in 3D tasks.
problem_solved: Most VLMs are trained on 2D images and struggle with tasks that require precise 3D spatial understanding, such as depth reasoning, viewpoint changes, and geometric inference.
method: Learns Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) to encode high-level 3D geometric priors from RGB video.
Uses explicit geometry representations to provide more concrete spatial structure alongside the implicit cues.
Combines both geometry types in a unified VLM framework to improve 3D reasoning without relying on specialized 3D sensors.
impact: This approach can improve how VLMs handle robotics, AR/VR, autonomous systems, and embodied AI tasks where 3D understanding matters. For practitioners, it offers a path to make existing multimodal models more spatially intelligent using video data.

paper_title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
paper_authors: Wenhao Li, Xueying Jiang, Quanhao Qian, Deli Zhao, Ran Xu
